case_studies.title: IDP AutoOpt: Agent-Driven Optimization of Document Processing Pipeline Configurations
case_studies.abstract: We present IDP AutoOpt, an autonomous LLM agent that discovers high-performing configurations for intelligent document processing (IDP) pipelines. Tuning IDP prompts, models, OCR settings, and schemas jointly currently costs domain specialists 20 to 80+ person-hours per document type and does not scale as enterprises add document classes. IDP AutoOpt runs a closed loop: it scores a configuration on a small labeled set, diagnoses field-level errors, generates targeted edits, and re-evaluates, guided by human-authored domain skills that encode production expertise. Across extraction, classificat
case_studies.summary: IDP AutoOpt solves the problem of optimizing document processing pipeline configurations, which currently requires significant manual effort from domain specialists. The researchers built an autonomous agent that can discover high-performing configurations, reducing the need for manual tuning. The result is a more efficient and scalable process for intelligent document processing.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage document processing pipelines, here is what to do: check if your current configuration tuning process is manual and time-consuming, consider implementing an autonomous optimization tool like IDP AutoOpt, and assess the potential benefits of reduced manual effort and improved scalability.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High scores due to strong IT relevance, novel application of LLMs in IDP, and significant potential impact on enterprise IT operations. The IDP AutoOpt system addresses a pressing need for automation in document processing, with significant value potential over 90 days.

case_studies.title: TraceCoder: Explainable and Auditable Code Generation with Position-Key Snippet Versioning
case_studies.abstract: Contemporary LLM-based coding agents produce code as black-box outputs: the rationale behind each line is hidden, the evolution of the code through benchmark-driven repair is ephemeral, and post-hoc auditing is impossible. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of explaining and auditing code generated by AI tools, by creating a system called TraceCoder that records and visualises the history of code changes. TraceCoder allows for full provenance queries and provides a browser-based visualisation tool. The result is more transparent and trustworthy code generation.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI-powered coding tools, here is what to do: review your current auditing processes, consider implementing a similar snippet-history schema, and assess the potential for integrating a visualisation tool like TraceCoder to improve code transparency.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novel code generation concept directly relevant to IT infrastructure and AI deployment. However, it may not be of immediate value to IT engineers or consultants for the next 90 days.

case_studies.title: From Backlog Items to Security Guidance: Towards Continuous Security Compliance
case_studies.abstract: Continuous software engineering in regulated domains requires engineering teams to address security throughout the development lifecycle. Yet making security requirements explicit in backlog items is still problematic. Engineers must instead infer security relevance of backlog items from brief, free-form descriptions and often lack timely guidance on applicable requirements. We present an NLP-based backlog enrichment system that detects security-relevant backlog items and links them to relevant security requirements. The approach combines a security-relevance classifier with a retrieval-augmen
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of making security requirements explicit in software development by building an NLP-based system that detects security-relevant backlog items and links them to relevant security requirements. The system combines a security-relevance classifier with a retrieval-augmentation module to provide timely guidance on applicable requirements. The result is improved continuous security compliance in regulated domains.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud-based software development, here is what to do: review your current backlog management process to identify potential security gaps, consider implementing an NLP-based enrichment system to detect security-relevant items, and ensure your team has access to timely security guidance and requirements. This flags a risk: if your organisation uses agile development methodologies, check your backlog items for security relevance immediately. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work outside of software development.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty in using NLP to detect security-relevant backlog items, but IT relevance is moderate. Value in 90 days is high due to automation potential.

case_studies.title: StealthBench: Measuring Operational Stealth in Autonomous Offensive-Security Agents
case_studies.abstract: Stealth, the discipline of achieving an objective without revealing your presence, capabilities, or collected intelligence, is what separates sophisticated operators from detectable ones. Elite security researchers and advanced persistent threats achieve their objectives unnoticed; autonomous agents increasingly inherit the same offensive tasks, but do they inherit the tradecraft? We introduce StealthBench,a benchmark that measures operational stealth in autonomous offensive-security agents across six operational security (OPSEC) dimensions. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of measuring how well autonomous security agents can operate without being detected, by building a benchmark called StealthBench. The result is a tool that can measure operational stealth across six dimensions. This benchmark helps evaluate the effectiveness of autonomous security agents in maintaining stealth.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage autonomous security agents, here is what to do: review your agents' operational security configurations, use StealthBench to measure their stealth capabilities, and adjust their settings to improve their ability to operate undetected. This flags a risk: if your org uses autonomous agents for security tasks, check their stealth capabilities immediately to ensure they are not detectable. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to security teams using autonomous agents.
case_studies.score_reasoning: StealthBench may interest IT engineers in security, but novelty is limited. Directly affects IT by providing a benchmark for measuring operational stealth in autonomous security agents. Not actionable in 90 days.

case_studies.title: PAUSE: A User-Centric Benchmark for Personal AI Assistants in Unified Service Environments
case_studies.abstract: Personal AI assistants are increasingly deployed as task-oriented, tool-augmented agents that operate within unified service environments to support everyday user activities. In realistic settings, such assistants must reason over persistent user state, respect user-specific configurations and permissions, and sustain long-horizon, constraint-aware interactions across multiple services. Existing benchmarks, however, often fragment service contexts or abstract away user state, limiting their ability to evaluate user-centric personal assistant behavior in realistic service settings. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating personal AI assistants in realistic unified service environments. The researchers built a user-centric benchmark called PAUSE to test personal AI assistants. The result is a more realistic way to evaluate how well these assistants support everyday user activities.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on evaluating personal AI assistants rather than managing cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty 5: Introduces a new benchmark, but does not reveal anything surprising. IT Relevance 5: Focuses on AI assistants in unified service environments, but does not directly affect how IT engineers work. Value 10: Provides a framework that could be used to evaluate personal AI assistants, but its practical application is unclear.
